citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility has not provided veterinary care to a gilt with an umbilical hernia. There is a soft, pendulous swelling
extending away from near the umbilical area that is approximately the size of a tennis ball. The pig is still eating and
drinking and does not appear affected by the swelling. Licensee noted the hernia prior to inspection and did not
communicate the issue with their attending veterinarian. The licensee states he did not proceed with treatment due to her
potential use in a research study and in hopes that it would repair on its own.
Failure to address the umbilical hernia can result in further complications such as intestinal entanglement which will
impact the animal’s well-being. Correct by having the gilt examined by your veterinarian to determine the best course of
treatment.
Correct by 11/6/26

The facility is not cleaning the primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent contamination of the pigs contained
therein. An outdoor pen consisting of two grower pigs contains a moderate accumulation of fresh and old manure
alongside its walls. Both pigs were observed with manure on both front and rear hocks and along their face and ventrum.
The concrete walls and flooring have a buildup of brown organic debris and excreta. Additionally, PVC pipes used to
deliver feed directly into the hog feeders have caked on layers of dirt and debris.
Regular cleaning of enclosures is necessary to help reduce the spread of disease, pests, and unpleasant odors. Excreta
shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent contamination of animals contained therein
and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.
Correct by 11/6/26
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
